hypotheses.justification: The proof uses `NeZero N` only to obtain `HeckeEis.ZQAux.instGroupFG_Gamma0 N` (finite generation of `Gamma0 N`, proved via finite index, which needs N ≠ 0). For N = 0 the result still holds. Mathlib defines `Gamma0 N` as `{g | (g 1 0 : ZMod N) = 0}`, and `ZMod 0 = ℤ`, so `Gamma0 0` is the upper-triangular subgroup of SL(2,ℤ). From det = ad = 1 we get a = d = ±1, so each element equals a • T^(a·b) with T = `ModularGroup.T`. Hence `Gamma0 0` is generated by the two elements `⟨T, _⟩` and `⟨-1, _⟩` and is finitely generated (it is abelian, isomorphic to ℤ × ℤ/2). New proof: split on N = 0. When N ≠ 0, use the existing instance. When N = 0, give the explicit two-element generating set, whose closure is everything by the short argument above. Everything else is unchanged: `coeffCocycles_eq_of_eqOn` only needs `Subgroup.closure s = ⊤`, and `Module.Finite.of_injective` into the Noetherian module `S → BinaryForm ℤ n` does not involve N. So `Module.Finite ℤ (coeffParabolicCocycles …)` holds for every N.
